Counsel for Applicant :- Anand Narayan Singh,Arvind Kumar Jauhari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.

1. Heard Shri Anand Narayan Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Onkar Nath Pandey,
brief holder for the State and perused the record.

2. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No.565 of 2020, under Sections-498A, 306 I.P.C., Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.- Motipur,
District Bahraich.
3. This is the second bail application.
The first bail application was rejected on 30.03.2022 by coordinate Bench of this Court.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that after rejection of first bail application, fact witnesses PW1 and PW2 brothers of deceased and PW3 mother of the deceased have been examined before the trial court therefore, new cause of action has arisen.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that PW1 brother, complainant of the case has not supported the prosecution case in his cross examination.
He has deposed that tahrir was written by his brother and the same was signed without reading.
He also denied the allegation of dowry demand levelled against the applicant and his family members.
He further deposed that his sister fell down from rickshaw and received injuries due to which he died.

1 not record his statement and denied the entire version of 161 Cr.P.C. as well as version of FIR.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel has invited attention of this Court towards the statements of PW2 brother Ajay and mother of the deceased, who have not supported the prosecution case and both have been declared hostile.

It is submitted that there is no possibility that trial will be concluded in near future,
therefore, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
6.
Shri Anand Narayan Singh, learned counsel has made statement at Bar that applicant has no previous criminal history and is languishing in jail since 24.07.2021.
7. Learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that PW1, PW2 brothers of the deceased and PW3 mother of the deceased have not supported the prosecution case.

8. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and after hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the fact that both PW1 PW2 brothers of deceased and PW3 mother of deceased, all family members have not supported the prosecution case and have become hostile, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

9. Let the applicant, Keshri Nath Alias Mahendra Nath be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
